summary: Returns the top element of a stack of std::unique_ptr<T> while transferring ownership to the caller via move semantics. The moved-from internal slot is then popped from the underlying vector. Strong exception guarantee — if the move-construction of the return value throws, the stack remains unchanged.

outputs.name: result
outputs.semantic: Sole owner of the element formerly on top of the stack. The caller is responsible for keeping it alive or letting it auto-destroy at scope exit.

invariants.claim: After return, the stack's size is decreased by exactly 1 — or pop is a precondition violation (empty stack; see UB-1).
The returned unique_ptr's stored pointer equals the pointer that was on top of the stack at entry; no copy of the pointee occurs.

If T's destructor throws (which violates the standard's noexcept assumption for destructors), behaviour is implementation-defined; the stack is left in an unspecified state. The routine itself does not invoke ~T directly.

object_lifetimes.subject: return value (std::unique_ptr<T>)
object_lifetimes.policy: Caller becomes sole owner. The stack relinquishes its claim; the moved-from slot is then popped. Java translation: AutoCloseable + try-with-resources. .NET translation: IDisposable + using.

object_lifetimes.subject: internal storage (std::vector<std::unique_ptr<T>>)
object_lifetimes.policy: The vector is a member; pop mutates it in-place. No allocation; no deallocation beyond the pop_back.

exception_contracts.contract: If the move-construction of the return value throws (it shouldn't for unique_ptr — move is noexcept), the stack is unchanged. If pop_back throws (it doesn't for std::vector), the stack invariant is preserved. C# translation: try/return-by-value; Java translation: same; both targets benefit from this guarantee verbatim.

undefined_behaviors.trigger: Calling pop on an empty stack. The implementation does not check size; back() on an empty vector is undefined behavior.

The popped slot is `std::move`d into the return value, then immediately popped from the vector. If the caller's flow somehow re-references that slot through aliased iterators, the moved-from unique_ptr is in a valid-but-unspecified state.

side_effects.description: Mutates the stack's internal vector — size decreases by 1; the popped slot is destroyed by pop_back (but its unique_ptr was already moved out, so no double-destroy).

edge_cases.description: Stack contains exactly one element. After pop, size is 0; subsequent pop is UB-1.
edge_cases.behavior: Functions correctly; the size becomes 0 cleanly.

edge_cases.description: T is a non-movable type (e.g. const-qualified). Compile fails because unique_ptr<T> requires T to be destructible AND the return type implies a move.
edge_cases.behavior: Compile error; SFINAE not applied — the user gets a templated error message.

open_questions.question: Should the translation make 'pop on empty' explicit (.NET: throw InvalidOperationException; Java: throw NoSuchElementException) or preserve the precondition semantics? The Borrowed-vs-Unique ownership story translates cleanly; only this defensive guard is at the SME's discretion.
